hypotheses.reasoning: Until 18:38, redis-cache shows steady hit ratios of about 95% and catalog-db shows only routine checkpoint and vacuum lines. At 18:38:02 redis-cache restarted after a node replacement and found no RDB snapshot, so it came back with 0 keys (#3116); it logs nothing after that. Within 30s search-api reports a 98% cache miss ratio (baseline 6%) and sends every lookup to catalog-db (#3196, #3326). That is a cache stampede. catalog-db then climbs to 481 and later 498 of 500 connections with CPU at 96-100% (#3233, #3355), and simple point lookups on products take 4-8s (#3502, #3631). search-api product queries start timing out at 5000ms (#3684, #3764). web-bff 504s on /search start at 18:40:24 and match the alert. The cache restart alone was survivable; the damage came from every miss going to the database. Noise I ruled out: the status-poller timeouts against the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint, metrics-agent exporter drops, the audit-consumer poison message from 18:40:33 (it starts after the onset and doesn't touch the search path), one 3s catalog-svc blip at 18:34, one slow audit_log seq scan, and a GC pause in index-worker.
catalog-db running out of connections and CPU could be read as resource exhaustion. But it only happens after the cache was wiped, so it is a symptom of the stampede.
audit-consumer keeps crashing on msg-853789. This starts after the search latency began and is on an unrelated path.

verdict.recommendedAction: Reduce the load on catalog-db: rate-limit or shed search traffic, and add single-flight/request coalescing on cache misses in search-api so only one request per key reloads from the database. Warm redis-cache with hot product keys. Then enable RDB/AOF persistence or replica failover on redis-cache so a node replacement doesn't bring it back empty. Separately, fix audit-consumer: dead-letter msg-853789 and its recursion bug.
